issues.body: # Add row display controls to State timeline This issue proposes row display controls to the State timeline panel so dashboards with many or few timeline rows can be configured more predictably. ## Why is this needed State timeline currently scales rows to fit the panel height. This works for some data shapes, but causes poor readability in common cases: - Many rows are compressed until labels and state bands are difficult to read. - Few rows can become visually stretched and waste panel space. - Users who want consistent row sizing need to manually tune panel height or pagination. ## Who is this feature for? Dashboard authors and viewers who use State timeline panels with many series, sparse series, or dashboards where consistent row sizing and readable timelines are important. ## Related issues This addresses existing State timeline feature requests: - Fixes https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/94728 - Requests vertical scrolling for State timeline when many series are present. - Notes that the previous `Row height` option controlled bar fill as a percentage, not the actual row height. This PR renames that option to `Row fill` to better describe its behavior. - Helps with https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/96500 - Requests row-height control for State timeline rows. - This PR adds panel-level fixed row height. Per-series row height overrides remain out of scope. This also relates to older dashboard sizing discussions: - Related to https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/10325 - Requests panels that can grow based on content height. - This PR implements that behavior narrowly for State timeline through `Auto height`. - Related to https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/1141 - Discusses auto-adjusting panel height for different display sizes. - This PR does not add responsive dashboard-wide resizing, but gives State timeline a content-aware height mode. - Related to https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/14334 - Requests minimum panel height support. - This PR does not add a generic `minHeight` grid property, but fixed row height plus scroll mode improves usability when panel height is constrained. ## What changed This adds or updates three panel options under State timeline settings: - **Row display** - **Scroll**: keeps the panel height fixed and scrolls rows internally. This is the default for new State timeline panels. - **Page**: keeps existing pagination behavior, with optional fixed row height. - **Auto height**: grows the dashboard grid item to fit visible rows. - **Row height** - New optional fixed row height in pixels. - Available for Scroll, Page, and Auto height modes. - Existing dashboards keep the previous fit-to-panel behavior unless this is set. - **Row fill** - Renamed from the previous `Row height` option. - Controls the fraction of each row filled by the state bar, allowing visual gaps between rows. - Available for Scroll, Page, and Auto height modes. ## Implementation notes - The State timeline panel computes a fixed chart height from visible row count and configured fixed row height. - Page mode caps the chart height so the pagination footer remains visible when fixed row height is set. - Auto height dispatches a small browser event consumed by dashboard grid items. - Dashboard grid items convert the requested pixel height into Grafana grid rows using the existing grid cell height and vertical margin constants. - Leaving Auto height resets the grid item back to its original height. ## Screenshots ### Options New Display mode options, including fixed `Row height` and renamed `Row fill`. State timeline options with Scroll row display selected (Options are the same as for Auto Height) State timeline options with Pages row display selected ### Panel behavior **Scroll mode** keeps many rows readable inside a fixed panel by making the panel content scrollable. Many State timeline rows displayed with internal scrolling **Page mode** remains compatible with fixed row height and keeps pagination visible. State timeline Page mode with fixed row height and pagination **Auto height** shrinks the panel when only a few rows are visible, avoiding empty space below the timeline. Auto height with a few State timeline rows Auto height grows the panel so all rows are visible, shifting panels below it. Auto height with many State timeline rows ## Tests - Added State timeline panel tests for: - Auto height dispatching resize updates, not dirtying dashboard user changes. - Scroll mode using internal scrolling without resizing the dashboard grid. - Page mode supporting fixed row height without resizing the dashboard grid. - Page mode keeping pagination visible when fixed row height is set. - Added dashboard grid item test for: - Converting State timeline fixed height updates into grid row height changes. - Resetting to the original grid height when Auto height is disabled. ## Verification - `make gen-cue` - `git diff --check` - `yarn eslint public/app/core/constants.ts public/app/plugins/panel/state-timeline/StateTimelinePanel.tsx public/app/plugins/panel/state-timeline/StateTimelinePanel.test.tsx public/app/plugins/panel/state-timeline/module.tsx public/app/plugins/panel/state-timeline/styles.ts public/app/features/dashboard-scene/scene/layout-default/DashboardGridItem.tsx public/app/features/dashboard-scene/scene/layout-default/DashboardGridItem.test.tsx` - `yarn jest --no-watch public/app/plugins/panel/state-timeline/StateTimelinePanel.test.tsx public/app/features/dashboard-scene/scene/layout-default/DashboardGridItem.test.tsx` # Attention needed I created PR combining all the changes (https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/132284), but I agree the original PR combined panel behavior, panel schema changes, and dashboard layout behavior, made the blast radius too large. I’d like to split the work and get maintainer alignment before opening smaller PRs. There are two related but separable parts: 1. Panel-local row display controls: - Fixed row height in pixels. - Internal vertical scrolling. - Pagination compatibility. - Rename the existing visual “Row height” option to “Row fill” because it controls bar fill percentage, not actual row height. And term "Row height" will be used for new functionality described above. 2. Dashboard layout auto height: - Optional mode where the State timeline panel asks the dashboard grid item to resize to fit visible rows. - This is useful when users want all rows visible without internal scrolling. - This part touches dashboard layout, dirty tracking, and serialization, so it has a larger review/rollback surface. ## Proposed split I propose splitting into smaller PRs: 1. Rename existing “Row height” visual option to “Row fill” with migration only, no behavior change. 2. Add fixed row height and scroll/page row display behavior inside State timeline only, without dashboard layout changes. 3. Separately discuss/implement Auto height behind an experimental feature flag if maintainers agree with the approach. ## Questions for maintainers - Is the panel-only fixed row height + scroll/page behavior acceptable as a first step? - Should the schema changes use the proposed fields, or would you prefer different option names/shape before they become persisted schema? - Is Auto height acceptable as a State timeline feature, or should this wait for a more general dashboard layout mechanism? - If Auto height is acceptable, should it be behind a new experimental feature flag? - Is a State timeline-specific browser event to request runtime grid height acceptable, provided it does not dirty the dashboard and does not persist runtime height changes?
issues.title: StateTimeline: Improve State timeline row sizing and display modes

issues.body:
## Summary

`jsonData.manageAlerts: false` does not actually prevent a data source from being used
to create alert rules. There is no working, reliable way to disable alerting for a data
source from the UI.

## Problem

The data source config editor exposes a "Manage alert rules in Alerting UI" switch that
is backed by `jsonData.manageAlerts` (`AlertingSettings` in `packages/grafana-ui`).
The expectation is that turning this switch off fully disables alert management for the
data source, so users can no longer create or edit alert rules against it.

In practice, `jsonData.manageAlerts: false` only affects external rules sources:
`isDataSourceManagingAlerts` / `getRulesDataSources`
(`public/app/features/alerting/unified/utils/datasource.ts`) filter the list of external
(Prometheus/Loki-flavored) rules sources. It does **not** stop a user from manually
creating a Grafana-managed alert rule whose query targets that data source through the
Alerting UI.

This matters when a data source is meant to be managed outside Grafana. A concrete case
is the VictoriaLogs data source
([victorialogs-datasource](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/victorialogs-datasource)):
logs-based alerts are often managed externally via `VMRule` + `vmalert` using LogsQL,
with Grafana acting only as a read-only client. See
[victorialogs-datasource#727](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/victorialogs-datasource/issues/727).
Even with `jsonData.manageAlerts: false`, a user can still manually create a
VictoriaLogs-backed alert rule in the UI, which can produce expensive LogsQL rules that
are hard to review and put continuous load on VictoriaLogs.

## Problem

`jsonData.manageAlerts: false` should fully disable alert creation for the data source,
but it does not. Concretely:

- Provisioning a data source with `jsonData.manageAlerts: false` still allows manually
  creating an alert rule for that data source via the Alerting UI.
- There is no setting that reliably prevents a data source from being chosen as the query
  target of a Grafana-managed alert rule.

## Expected behavior

Provide a way to fully disable alerting for a data source from the UI, such that:

- The "Manage alert rules in Alerting UI" toggle, when off, prevents the data source from
  being used to create or edit any alert rule (both data source-managed and Grafana-managed).
- This behavior should also apply to any data source that opts out of alerting, regardless
  of whether its `plugin.json` declares `alerting: true`.
issues.title: Feature request: Allow disabling alerting for a data source so it cannot be used to create alert rules

## Current status

Current prototype: #133050. Closed working PR #132542 and branch #130506 below are historical context, not shipped implementation. The approach below remains a proposal; pinning's representation is not settled. Sharing/promotion is tracked in #133139.

Column pinning is the one refreshed-table column interaction left out of the ad-hoc transformation stage (https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/132542), because it is the only one that isn't purely a data change.

A pin is two things at once:

- a **reorder** — pinned columns have to form a leading run, because react-data-grid only freezes a leading run
- a **panel-option change** — the frozen column count, `frozenColumns.left`

Only the first half is expressible as `organize`. Shipping just that half would be lossy (unpinning has no memory of the prior order) and would leak a purely visual affordance into everything downstream that reads the post-ad-hoc frames — CSV download, Inspect Data.

**Proposed approach:** a "hidden" transformation type whose effect is to tweak panel options and which is deliberately not listed in the transformations UI. A pin then becomes a single ad-hoc entry carrying both halves. The same mechanism is what brings the persisted `sortBy` option into reach (see the sorting issue).

**Open questions for that design:**

- How does such a type interact with the transformations editors' wholesale-replace model, once it can be promoted into `panel.transformations`?
- Can an options-mutating transformation be made idempotent enough to re-run on every pipeline pass?

**Also in scope:** adding `pinnable` to `TableFieldOptions` alongside `filterable` / `sortable` / `reorderable` / `hideable`. It was deliberately left out of #132542 so it could be built against real behaviour rather than added speculatively.

The pin UI already exists on the working branch (https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/130506) — the handler is simply not passed, which takes the menu item with it. Two things that come back with it: seeding the pinned set from the column catalog rather than the post-hide fields, and pruning pinned names on reconciliation instead of wiping them.

Depends on the shared ad-hoc foundation in #133138. Part of grafana/grafana-org#1000.

Design doc: [Table Ad-Hoc Transformations](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ixPSx2-vh6-6PUFMcFAKddoKICqPvwCYYyXzFzHHWQU/edit)
issues.title: Table: column pinning

<!-- Please only use this template for submitting feature requests -->

**Why is this needed**:

The v2beta1 dashboard schema (dashboardSectionVariables feature toggle) lets a TabsLayout tab declare its own local variables, scoped so they're invisible outside that tab. But annotations (spec.annotations[]) can only be defined dashboard-wide - DashboardTabsLayoutTabSpec has no annotations field.

This creates a silent failure mode: if an annotation's query filters on a tab-scoped variable, the variable is unresolved at the dashboard-global annotation's evaluation point, so the annotation never renders anywhere, on any panel. There's no error. The underlying metric query can be verified as correct in Explore, the annotation looks correctly configured in the UI, and it just silently produces nothing. I only found the cause by noticing the same annotation config worked on a second dashboard where the equivalent variable was dashboard-global instead of tab-scoped, then confirming via the devtools inspecting the request made and also via the OpenAPI schema that tab specs simply have no annotations field.


**What would you like to be added**:

Either of these would resolve it:
1. Add an annotations field to DashboardTabsLayoutTabSpec, so an annotation can be scoped to the tab whose local variables it depends on - mirroring how variables already works per-tab.
2. If full tab-scoped annotations are out of scope, at minimum surface a warning when a dashboard-global annotation query references a variable that's tab-scoped and therefore unresolvable at evaluation time (e.g. a warning icon on the annotation list item, or a dashboard-JSON validation warning) instead of failing silently.

**Who is this feature for?**

Anyone using TabsLayout with per-tab (section) variables (something the dashboardSectionVariables toggle explicitly enables) who also wants a restart/event/deploy-style annotation overlay scoped to that same tab's selection. Currently this combination is a dead end with no diagnostic signal.
issues.title: Support tab-scoped (section) annotations in the v2beta1 dashboard schema

### What happened?

There is no way to restrict a user's ability to run arbitrary queries against a datasource.

This essentially delegitimizes any sort of actual permission restriction mechanism Grafana does expose. There is almost no point in trying to restrict dashboards a user can see when if they have access to view any they will be able to run any arbitrary query they want effectively making any sort of actual dashboard restriction entirely moot.


There's certainly been issues about it going back for a while which should indicate there is some level of importance to this request.

• #6180, opened in 2016
• #48313, opened in 2022
•  #114769 , opened in 2025

I know that this has been mentioned as by design/intentional in other issues but the way the roles and permissions are documented  does not at all give the impression that all users who can view any subset of dashboards can actually run all the queries and data that power all dashboards using that data source plus any arbitrary query they want.

The response to these items seem somewhat dismissive. to me At least with Azure Managed Grafana, there is only a singular Managed Identity exposed that you can use to grant access to data sources. There is NOT any way to setup finer grained perms for various identities and data sources on the same Grafana instance because you only have access to one. This means the only way to actually have finer grained perms for the identity would be to make multiple Grafana instances which isn't scalable and still invalidates the entire intent behind trying to restrict what dashboards users can actually see on a single instance.


### What did you expect to happen?

That if I only allow a user to view certain dashboards using Managed Identity data sources that they would only be able to run the queries powering those dashboards and not any arbitrary query.

### Did this work before?

Unsure, but based on history of issues it seems like it has been going on for a long time.

### How do we reproduce it?

1. Setup any data source with Managed Identity authentication in Azure Managed Grafana
2. Give a user any means to actually view a dashboard and have it function that uses this data source (even with as tightly scoped of perms as Grafana allows)
3. User can run any arbitrary query against the data source via the Grafana APIs

**Why is this needed**:

Grafana Assistant and related agent/MCP paths can drive powerful workflows (dashboards, queries, navigation, and eventually remediations / admin-style actions). For privileged actions, teams need a host-side signed proof that an approval gate ran **before** the action executes.

Vault/IAM style controls answer who may act. AffixIO answers whether a specific host-side **action** gate completed (signed yes/no). It is not person/age/KYC. PII stays on the host.

**What would you like to be added**:

An integration path (docs and/or thin example) to sit AffixIO in front of privileged Assistant / agent-driven remediations and admin actions:

1. Before a privileged tool/admin/remediation action runs, require AffixIO host-side approval
2. Proceed only on signed yes
3. Optionally attach the attestation to audit/ops context

Install:

```bash
npm i affixio
# optional local MCP (stdio)
npm i @affixio/mcp@0.1.0
```

Links:

- https://www.affix-io.com/
- https://hub.affix-io.com/onboarding/

Not asking for a full AffixIO middleware wrap inside Grafana core. Prefer a docs note or community example on the Assistant / MCP / remediation surface if maintainers want it.

**Who is this feature for?**

Platform/security teams running Grafana Assistant (on-prem or Cloud) where agents can trigger remediations or admin actions, and need portable host-side action attestation alongside existing RBAC.

Happy to contribute a minimal example if that is welcome. Will wait for maintainer direction before any PR.

**Why is this needed**:

The current Node Graph visualization provides ways to customize arc colors and supports a `highlighted` state for nodes, but there is no way to dynamically set the fill/background color of an individual node based on a field value.

This becomes a limitation when a Node Graph is used to visualize the health or status of a service journey.

For example, in a service journey, each node may represent a step such as `initialize_score`, `validate_otp`, or `end_state`. The success rate of each step can be different, and it is useful to immediately communicate this status through the node's fill color.

For example:

- Green fill → healthy / high success rate
- Yellow/orange fill → degraded / medium success rate
- Red fill → unhealthy / low success rate

Currently, `highlighted` can indicate a node state, but it is a boolean value and therefore cannot represent multiple status levels or dynamically map a numeric metric to different colors.

Without node fill color, users have to rely on arcs, labels, or additional statistics to understand the state of each node, which makes the visualization less effective for service-health and journey monitoring.

**What would you like to be added**:

Add support for a configurable **node fill/background color** in the Node Graph visualization.

Ideally, the fill color should be configurable from a data field, allowing the color of each node to be determined independently based on its value.

For example, a field such as:

```text
node_color
issues.title: add filling color to node graph

**Why is this needed**:

Most of Grafana's histograms only define classic buckets: on main (ea76988a41b), 114 of the 186 histogram definitions under `pkg/` and `apps/` set no `NativeHistogramBucketFactor`, so Prometheus setups that scrape native histograms still store each of their buckets as its own series. On a 12.4.11 instance, the classic-only histograms it exposes account for about 3,000 of its 12,800 series, and six make up 2,250: `grafana_datasource_request_duration_seconds` (510), `grafana_plugin_request_duration_seconds` (494), `grafana_alerting_request_duration_seconds` (462), `grafana_plugin_request_duration_milliseconds` (357), `grafana_caching_query_caching_request_duration_seconds` (221) and `grafana_plugin_request_size_bytes` (204). `grafana_datasource_response_size_bytes` has had native buckets since #87962, but the request-duration histogram defined next to it in `pkg/infra/httpclient/httpclientprovider/datasource_metrics_middleware.go` still does not.

Converting them at scrape time with Prometheus's `convert_classic_histograms_to_nhcb` cuts the series count but keeps the coarse classic buckets, and Prometheus will not send the result over remote write 1.0 (it drops them as `nhcb_in_rw1_not_supported`), so it is not a substitute.

**What would you like to be added**:

The native settings #87962 used (`NativeHistogramBucketFactor: 1.1`, `NativeHistogramMaxBucketNumber: 100`, `NativeHistogramMinResetDuration: time.Hour`) on those histograms, keeping the existing `Buckets` so classic-only scrapers see no change. I can open the PR for the six above.

**Who is this feature for?**

Operators who scrape Grafana with native histograms enabled, for lower cardinality and finer latency percentiles.
issues.title: Instrumentation: enable native histograms on the remaining classic-only histograms

issues.body:
If you run several Grafana instances against a shared backend, the backend's access logs can't tell them apart, because every instance sends `Grafana/<version>`. `[dataproxy] user_agent` (#63769) solves this for in-process data sources (`http_client_provider.go:33`, `ds_proxy.go:274`) by letting you tag each instance. External backend plugins never get the setting.

### Current behavior

Since grafana/grafana-plugin-sdk-go#1602, plugins that use the SDK `httpclient` send:

```
Grafana/<version> (<os>; <arch>) <plugin-id>/<plugin-version>
```

The `Grafana/<version> (<os>; <arch>)` prefix comes from the plugin context, which Grafana builds from the build version in `base_plugincontext.go:63`. Nothing in the config can change it:

- `pluginconfig/request.go` passes keys like `ResponseLimit` and `SQLRowLimit` to plugins, but there's no user agent key.
- The plugin-context user agent has to match `^Grafana/<semver> \(<os>; <arch>\)$`, and `ConvertFromProtobuf.UserAgent` returns nil for anything else. So you can't pass a value like `Grafana/13.2.2 my-fleet/1` through that field.

Plugins built without build info are a separate case. `UserAgentMiddleware` returns early without setting the header, so the request goes out as `Go-http-client/1.1`.

### Proposal

1. Add an opt-in `[plugins] user_agent` setting, empty by default.
2. When it's set, Grafana includes it in the plugin request config. When it isn't, Grafana sends nothing extra.
3. In the SDK, `UserAgentMiddleware` uses the configured value instead of the plugin-context user agent, and still appends ` <plugin-id>/<plugin-version>`. It doesn't add `<os>; <arch>`, since the operator controls the whole prefix.
4. For example, with `user_agent = Grafana/13.2.2 my-fleet/1`, a request from `example-datasource` 2.4.0 sends `Grafana/13.2.2 my-fleet/1 example-datasource/2.4.0`.
5. If a plugin has no build info, the middleware sets just the configured value rather than leaving the header empty.
6. Grafana should reject values with control characters when it reads the setting.
7. If the setting isn't set, nothing changes.

### Open question

Should `[plugins] user_agent` fall back to `[dataproxy] user_agent` when it isn't set? A fallback lets one setting cover both in-process and plugin traffic, which is probably what most people want. Separate settings are more explicit, but you'd need two values to tag one instance. We don't have a strong preference, but it affects how the setting is shaped, so it's worth settling first.

### Scope and rollout

This doesn't cover `[dataproxy] forward_user_agent`, which appends the client's User-Agent. That could be a separate change.

The SDK change only applies to a plugin once that plugin upgrades the SDK and ships a release. Until then, some plugins will honor the setting and others will ignore it, and operators won't be able to tell which. Listing the minimum SDK version in the setting's docs would make that clear.

### Implementation

SDK change: grafana/grafana-plugin-sdk-go#1772. It needs to land and be released first, since Grafana uses the key constant from the SDK. The Grafana side is ready and will follow once an SDK release includes it.
issues.title: External backend plugins can't use a configured User-Agent

**Why is this needed**:

When saving changes to a file-provisioned dashboard with `allowUiUpdates: false`, users currently have no way to export pending changes in a portable format suitable for other Grafana instances. The Export dialog offers a "Share dashboard with another instance" toggle that removes instance-specific metadata (UIDs, namespaces, resource versions, grafana.app/* labels/annotations) and transforms data-source references—but this toggle is absent from the provisioned save dialog. Additionally, the Export dialog fetches the persisted dashboard state through the API rather than exporting pending changes, making it unusable when `allowUiUpdates: false` prevents persistence.

This creates a workflow gap: users can export pending changes from the save dialog, but cannot make those changes portable across instances.

**What would you like to be added**:

Add an optional toggle to the provisioned dashboard save dialog (similar to the Export dialog) that:
- Removes instance-specific metadata (UIDs, namespaces, resource versions, grafana.app/* labels/annotations)
- Optionally transforms data-source references to be portable across instances
- Applies this transformation to the pending (unsaved) changes, not just persisted state

This would allow users to:
1. Export pending dashboard changes in a format suitable for updating the provisioning source
2. Reuse the exported dashboard definition in another Grafana instance
3. Share dashboard definitions across different environments without instance-specific references

**Who is this feature for?**

- Operators managing file-provisioned dashboards across multiple Grafana instances
- Teams that maintain dashboards in version control and want to share them across staging/production environments
- Users who need to export dashboard changes without first saving them to the database (especially with `allowUiUpdates: false`)

**Why is this needed**:

Some self-managed deployments run Grafana inside a service mesh, such as Istio, where a sidecar next to Grafana encrypts traffic. The data source plugin sends traffic to the sidecar without TLS, and the mesh encrypts it between the proxies.

The ClickHouse data source [refuses to connect](https://github.com/grafana/clickhouse-datasource/blob/470e6edc5fb8a161761d6c7b7775dbb3a732050d/pkg/plugin/driver.go#L257-L258) when Forward OAuth Identity is on and the plugin does not set up TLS itself. The error is `JWT authentication requires a secure (TLS) connection`. A community pull request, grafana/clickhouse-datasource#2151, adds a data source setting to turn this check off. Tempo relaxed a similar check for basic auth over gRPC in #123026.

**What would you like to be added**:

A Grafana server setting that states that the network encrypts traffic outside Grafana. A data source that requires its own TLS before it forwards the signed-in user's OAuth identity, such as ClickHouse, can then skip that check. The setting must be off by default. A data source editor must not be able to turn it on alone, because the editor cannot see how the network handles traffic.

**Who is this feature for?**

Teams that run self-managed Grafana in a service mesh, or in another network that encrypts traffic outside the application. These teams use Forward OAuth Identity for per-user access control.

We want to know how many people need this. If you need it, please add a 👍 to this issue. In a comment, name your data source and say which component encrypts the traffic. Do not include hostnames or tokens.
issues.title: Data sources: Allow Forward OAuth Identity when a service mesh handles TLS

**Why is this needed**

The Infinity data source gained AWS SDK default-credential support in grafana/grafana-infinity-datasource#1538 (merged 2026-09-15, shipped in plugin 4.1.0). Its docs present **AWS SDK Default** as covering EKS IRSA and ECS task roles.

But #119772 forwards `AWS_ROLE_ARN`, `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`, the ECS container-credential variables and `AWS_REGION` only to plugins named in `[aws] forward_settings_to_plugins`, and `yesoreyeram-infinity-datasource` is not in the shipped default. On EKS, a provisioned Infinity data source with `authType: default` therefore has no web-identity token in its own plugin process, walks the SDK chain down to EC2 IMDS, and fails with:

```
failed to refresh cached credentials, no EC2 IMDS role found,
operation error ec2imds: GetMetadata, canceled, context deadline exceeded
```

Tested on Grafana 13.1.4 with Infinity 4.1.1. The Infinity Datasource workload had no AWS environment variables at all, while `grafana-amazonprometheus-datasource` and `grafana-opensearch-datasource` in the same pod did. Adding the plugin ID to `forward_settings_to_plugins` fixed it.

**What would you like to be added**

`yesoreyeram-infinity-datasource` appended to the default `forward_settings_to_plugins` in `conf/defaults.ini` and `conf/sample.ini`, following #124952 (`grafana-dynamodb-datasource`) and #108560 (`grafana-iot-twinmaker-datasource`).

**Who is this feature for?**

Anyone running Grafana on EKS or ECS who queries an AWS endpoint through Infinity -- S3, Cost Explorer, any SigV4 API. Today that works only with static access keys unless the operator discovers this setting and re-enumerates the list. #119235 and #119603 are the same IMDS failure for other plugins.
issues.title: Add yesoreyeram-infinity-datasource to the default [aws] forward_settings_to_plugins

issues.body:
**Why is this needed**:

We run Git Sync (Grafana 13.1.0 OSS, pure Git connection to GitLab) with two repositories, both `folderless`, sharing the same directory layout (one directory per project):

- repository A: dashboards edited by teams in the UI (`workflows: [write, branch]`);
- repository B: dashboards generated by CI from Jsonnet, read-only in Grafana (`workflows: []`), since any UI edit would be overwritten by the next render.

Every project that has dashboards in both repositories shows up twice at the root, as two folders with the same title (one marked "Read only"). Users have to look in two places for one project, and folder permissions have to be managed twice.

There is no way around it today:
- A folder is owned by a single repository: if repository B's `_folder.json` uses the UID of a folder created by repository A, the sync fails with `NewFolderManagedByOtherError` ([folders.go#L267](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/v13.1.0/pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/resources/folders.go#L267)).
- A resource's parent folder is always derived from its path in its own repository ([resources.go#L305](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/v13.1.0/pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/resources/resources.go#L305)), so repository B cannot target a folder of repository A.
- Switching repository B to the `folder` target only moves its tree under a wrapper folder: each project is still split in two (`payments` and `B/payments`).
- Merging both into a single repository loses the read-only guarantee, because read-only is a per-repository setting.

**What would you like to be added**:

Let a repository place its resources in a folder owned by another repository, without taking ownership of it. For example, when a directory of repository B has a `_folder.json` whose UID is already managed by repository A, use that folder as the parent instead of failing. Repository A keeps ownership of the folder (title, metadata, deletion); repository B only owns the dashboards it puts inside. Each dashboard keeps the read-only or editable behaviour of its own repository.

Open questions: what happens when repository A deletes a folder that still holds dashboards from repository B (block the deletion, or report it in the sync status); and the behaviour should probably be opt-in, for example a repository setting or an explicit field in `_folder.json`.

An alternative that would also solve our case: read-only paths inside a single repository (for example a glob such as `**/generated-*.json` that the UI refuses to save), so generated and hand-edited dashboards can share one repository and one folder tree.

**Who is this feature for?**

Teams that combine dashboards generated by a pipeline (Jsonnet, Grafonnet, Foundation SDK) with dashboards edited in the UI, and want both organised in the same per-project or per-team folder tree.
issues.title: Git Sync: allow several repositories to place dashboards in the same folder

## Add feature-flagged Azure Monitor Health Models query editor (subscription + health model selection)

### Summary
Add an "Azure Monitor Health Models" query type to the Azure Monitor data source behind a default-off feature flag. Users can pick a subscription and a Health Model. No health data is queried or visualised in this ticket.

### In scope
- Use the Health Models feature flag (default off) for discoverability only. The flag is not registered in this ticket.

- Add a backend resource endpoint in `pkg/tsdb/azuremonitor` that lists Health Models for a subscription. Call the ARM REST API through the existing resource proxy, as the other Azure Monitor resource calls do, using the data source's configured credentials. Use API version `v11`, handle ARM paging, and return errors as proper resource-handler errors.
- Add a `HealthModelsQueryEditor` component with two selectors:
  - **Subscription**: reuses the existing subscriptions lookup and supports template variables.
  - **Health Model**: shows `name (resource group)`, stores the full ARM resource ID, shows loading and error states, and clears when the subscription changes.
- Show the service option in the query header only when the Health Models feature flag is on. The editor and backend endpoint are not flag-checked.

### Out of scope
- Querying entities, relationships and the node graph ([ticket 2](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/135377)), and entity history and time series output ([ticket 3](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/135378)).

# Azure Monitor Health Models — Data Plane Plan

## Overview

This work extends the current Health Models prototype in Azure Monitor so it can support both **entity health snapshots** and **entity health history** using the Cloud Health data plane, while keeping model/entity metadata in ARM.

This plan is aligned with [grafana/grafana#135377](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/135377).

## What the prior code already does

- Lets the user select subscription + Health Model in the query editor.

## Plan

### 1) Discover and cache dataplane URL from ARM

- Use datasource-backed calls to reach the Health Models dataplane endpoint.
- Support the `getEntityHealth(dataplaneUrl, entity, timeline)` flow for snapshot reads.
- Store `azureHealthModels.dataplaneUrl` in the query model so we reuse it instead of rediscovering it every render.
- Clear and re-resolve the saved dataplane URL when subscription/model changes.
- Implement backend discovery from ARM Health Model metadata (`properties.dataPlaneUri`).
- Save/reuse the resolved dataplane URL per query execution.
- Keep persisted query field support (`azureHealthModels.dataplaneUrl`) so dashboards reuse the known endpoint.

### 2) Add explicit Health Models data functions

- `getEntityHealth(dataplaneUrl, entityName, timestamp)`
  - Calls dataplane snapshot endpoint for a single entity.
- `getEntityHistory(dataplaneUrl, entityName, startAt, endAt)`
  - Calls dataplane transitions endpoint and handles continuation paging.
- `getRelationships(modelResourceId, timestamp)`
  - Calls ARM relationships endpoint for the selected model/time context.

### 3) Keep auth separation correct

- ARM calls use existing ARM scope/token flow.
- Dataplane calls use Cloud Health scope: `https://data.cloudhealth.azure.com/.default`.
- Do not forward browser auth headers to upstream services.

### 4) Data returned to query pipeline

Return typed backend data for:

- Model metadata + dataplane URL
- Entity definitions
- Relationships
- Entity snapshot health
- Entity transition history

No visualization/frame rendering changes are required in this step; that follows in the downstream rendering task.

## Expected outcome

After this plan is completed:

- Queries can run snapshot and history flows with the right timestamp/range semantics.
- Relationship data is available for graph-style rendering.
- Dataplane endpoint discovery is minimized and reused safely.
- Dashboard refresh cadence drives when snapshot/history calls execute, without extra editor-only fetch loops.
issues.title: Fetch Health Model data from ARM and the data plane

## Transform Health Model data into node graph and time series frames

### Summary
Use the Go data-access layer from [grafana/grafana#135377](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/135377) to implement both Health Model result formats: a node graph at the dashboard end time and stepwise entity health history over the dashboard range.

This task owns frame construction, backend query execution, frontend query wiring, the Format selector and user documentation. It does not implement a second API client, authentication flow or paging loop.

### In scope
- Add the Go Health Models query handler and register it in `azuremonitor.go` alongside Metrics, Logs and Resource Graph. Use the existing Resource Graph handler as the integration pattern.
- Route frontend Health Models queries to backend execution.
- Interpolate `subscription` and `healthModelResourceId` before execution, and pass the resolved values and dashboard time range to the data layer.
- Add an optional `resultFormat` field to the query schema (`modelGraph` or `timeSeries`) and regenerate the TS and Go types:
  - Missing `resultFormat` defaults to `modelGraph`, preserving existing saved queries.
  - Unsupported format values return a clear per-query error.
- Add a Format selector to the Health Models editor, disabled until a model is selected:
  - **Health Model Graph** selects `modelGraph`.
  - **Health Model Entity History** selects `timeSeries`.
- Select the required data-layer operations for each format:
  - Graph: entity definitions, relationships and end-time health snapshots.
  - History: entity definitions, end-time health snapshots and transitions over the dashboard range.
  - Do not fetch transition history for graph queries.
- Keep frame builders independent of REST, authentication and transport response types. Their inputs are the plain Go types delivered by task 1.

#### Node graph frames
- Return named `nodes` and `edges` frames with the query's `refId` and the preferred visualisation type set to the node graph.
- Build nodes using:
  - `id`: entity name, not display name, because display names are not unique.
  - `title`: display name, falling back to entity name.
  - `subtitle` and `mainstat`: the data plane health state at the query end time.
  - `color`: fixed health-state colours for Healthy, Degraded, Unhealthy and Unknown.
- Use the Unknown colour for unrecognised state values. Do not substitute ARM health state.
- Build edges with `id`, `source` and `target` from relationship IDs and parent/child entity names.
- Include entities with no relationships. Drop edges whose source or target is absent from the model so ghost nodes are not drawn.
- Keep signal counts, alert severities and impact fields out of these frames.

#### Entity history frames
- Build one stepwise series per entity, covering the full dashboard range:
  - Sort transitions by time and include transitions inside the requested range.
  - Start at the range start with the state before the first in-range transition.
  - Add the new state at each transition.
  - End at the range end with the data plane snapshot state for that timestamp, not an unpinned current state.
  - If there are no transitions, use the end-time snapshot state throughout the range.
  - Handle transitions exactly on the range boundaries without duplicate or conflicting samples.
- Use stable health-state enum values: Healthy = `0`, Degraded = `1`, Unhealthy = `2`, Unknown = `3`. Map unrecognised state values to Unknown.
- Include time and health-state fields, enum text/colour metadata and step-after interpolation.
- Use the display name and entity name for the series label, and retain entity name as a stable identity.
- Propagate invalid-data and timestamp errors from the data layer instead of presenting a plausible but incomplete timeline.

#### Integration, tests and documentation
- Return actionable errors per query for failures from the data layer, preserving query attribution. Do not add fallback API calls or convert failures into empty successful frames.
- Keep the feature flag as a frontend discoverability control only; do not add a backend flag check.
- Add backend tests using a fake data-layer client for:
  - Format dispatch, the missing-format default and unsupported formats.
  - Exact node/edge frame fields, end-time health state, isolated nodes, duplicate display names, edge filtering and colour mapping.
  - History sorting, initial/final samples, range-boundary transitions, empty history, stepwise configuration and stable enum values.
  - Query time ranges, `refId` attribution, multiple targets, data-layer errors and avoiding history calls for graph queries.
- Add frontend tests for the Format selector, its disabled state, saved/default format behaviour, template interpolation and backend query routing.
- Reuse task 1's paging/authentication tests rather than duplicating their implementation here.
- Add user documentation for the Health Models editor, both formats, snapshot-versus-history time semantics and the ARM/data plane permissions required by the data source identity.

### Out of scope
- ARM or data plane client implementation, endpoint discovery, authentication, paging and request-concurrency control; these are delivered by task 1.
- Signal information, including healthy signal counts on nodes.
- Alert severities and impact information.
- Alerting support and backend feature-flag checks.

### Acceptance criteria
- Selecting **Health Model Graph**, or omitting the saved format, renders the node graph using health states at the dashboard end time.
- Each node's center shows its health state; isolated entities are present, duplicate display names do not merge nodes, and external relationships do not create ghost nodes.
- Selecting **Health Model Entity History** returns one stepwise series per entity covering the full dashboard range, including entities with no transitions.
- History start/end samples and boundary transitions are correct, and enum values match the documented stable mapping.
- Frame builders are testable with plain data and make no HTTP requests.
- Graph queries do not request history. Both formats use the data layer without reimplementing its authentication, paging or concurrency logic.
- Template variables work in the subscription and model fields, and failures are attributed to the appropriate query.
- The Format selector is disabled until a model is selected, and existing saved queries continue to return a node graph.
- Documentation covers both formats and the required permissions.
- Backend frame/query tests and frontend editor/routing tests pass.

issues.body:
## Problem

Text panel v2 suggests `${__data.fields.*}` macros in Once mode, but they require a row context and remain unresolved.

#133744 describes this mismatch. #133951 proposes using the row containing the first non-time field’s last non-null value as context for all field macros.

That introduces implicit coupling: one field determines which row every other field reads. Standard field reductions operate independently, so different fields’ last non-null values can come from different rows.

## Proposal

Allow data macros to specify a reducer explicitly. Each referenced field is reduced independently across its values, without assigning a shared row context.

Illustrative syntax, subject to compatibility with existing macro parsing and variable formatting:

```text
Latest CPU: ${__data.fields.cpu:reduce:lastNotNull}
Average CPU: ${__data.fields.cpu:reduce:mean}
Peak memory: ${__data.fields.memory:reduce:max}
```

Reuse Grafana’s existing reducers and field display formatting. Autocomplete should help users discover supported reducers.

## Expected behavior

Given:

| Time | CPU | Memory |
|---|---:|---:|
| 10:00 | 40 | 100 |
| 10:01 | 75 | null |
| 10:02 | null | 120 |

Independent `lastNotNull` reductions return CPU = `75` and Memory = `120`, despite coming from different rows.

Reduction does not establish a source row for other macros. In particular, reducers such as mean and sum have no corresponding source timestamp. Reducing the Time field independently must not imply that its result is the timestamp of another field’s reduced value.

## Acceptance criteria

- Explicit reducer macros resolve in Once mode without a row context.
- Each field reduces independently using existing Grafana reducer semantics.
- Reduced values respect field display configuration, including units and decimals.
- Autocomplete offers supported reducers and avoids suggesting bare row-dependent macros where no row context exists.
- Existing Per row macros retain their behavior.
- Tests cover independent last-non-null values, aggregate reducers, null/empty inputs, and display formatting.

## Scope

Start with Text panel v2. Shared macro support can be evaluated during implementation. Selecting a common row or exposing the source timestamp of a reduced value is outside this proposal.

Related: #133744, #133951.
issues.title: Text panel: Support explicit per-field reducers in data macros

## Problem

Text v2 blocks external content pending viewer consent. The affected panel should explain why content is missing through the shared panel warnings UI and provide a route into the consent flow.

The panel notices API landed in #134463 on October 26, 2026. It provides `PanelContext.notices` / `usePanelNotices`, warning severity, and custom status actions. Adopt this API for Text v2 consent warnings.

## Proposal

- Publish a panel-owned warning when the Text v2 sandbox reports external sources blocked pending consent.
- Explain that external content has been blocked and requires viewer approval, using the existing consent flow's safe origin summaries rather than full URLs.
- Provide a custom action such as **Review blocked content** that opens the existing consent flow for the affected panel. Opening the flow must not itself grant consent.
- Keep the warning synchronized with blocked-source and consent state. Clear it when no sources remain blocked, when the content changes to remove those sources, or when the panel unmounts. Recreate it if consent expires or is revoked and content becomes blocked again.
- Use a stable notice identity to avoid duplicates across rerenders, refreshes, and editor previews. Preserve the existing scope for repeated panel instances.
- Hide the Assistant CTA for this notice: viewer consent is the required action.

Use the merged API's UI conventions: notices appear in the panel status popover, while custom actions appear in the inspector. Decide how this entry point complements the dashboard consent banner without creating competing consent flows. Account for `grafana.newPanelQueryErrorsUI` being disabled so users retain a working consent entry point.

## Acceptance criteria

- A Text v2 panel with blocked external content shows a warning in the shared panel status UI.
- The warning explains the incomplete rendering and exposes an action that opens the appropriate consent flow.
- Granting consent updates the warning when blocked-source state changes; partial approval keeps a warning for remaining blocked sources.
- Content changes, consent expiration/revocation, panel removal, and repeated panel instances do not leave stale or duplicate warnings.
- Existing consent scope, persistence, and enforcement remain unchanged.
- Tests cover notice lifecycle, action routing, partial consent, repeated instances, and behavior with the panel errors/notices UI flag disabled.

## Implementation starting points

- `public/app/plugins/panel/text/v2/TextSandbox.tsx` reports blocked origins and clears them on cleanup.
- `public/app/plugins/panel/text/v2/TextNGPanel.tsx` supplies panel/dashboard consent context.
- `public/app/features/dashboard-scene/scene/sandbox-consent/` owns the existing consent flow.
- Follow the panel notice API documentation and examples added by #134463.

Parent epic: #128614.
issues.title: Text v2: Use panel notices for external-content consent warnings

<!-- Please only use this template for submitting feature requests -->

**Why is this needed**:

The heatmap panel's color options are limited to a fixed list of d3 schemes (plus single-color opacity). There is no way to define a color scale of your own. This is a problem for signed quantities where the neutral value must have a specific color and each direction a distinct hue, for example forecast bias (over- vs under-forecast) or deviation from a target.

I want a lead time x time-of-day heatmap of forecast bias with green at 0, blue toward negative and red toward positive values. None of the built-in schemes can do that:

- The diverging schemes (BrBG, PiYG, PRGn, PuOr, RdBu, RdGy, RdYlBu, RdYlGn, Spectral) are either neutral or yellow in the middle, or have green at one extreme.
- My workaround is the Turbo scheme with a deliberately asymmetric `color.min`/`color.max` (-100/120), so that 0 lands on Turbo's green. This works, but it distorts the scale and makes the legend misleading, because the same distance from zero shows a different shade in each direction.

Similar requests were closed without resolution when feature requests moved out of Discussions: #38227 (custom or inverted scheme) and #45634 (threshold-based colors).

**What would you like to be added**:

A way to define the color scale of a heatmap yourself. Preferred: a "Custom" color mode with a list of color stops, interpolated across the existing `steps`:

```json
"color": {
  "mode": "custom",
  "stops": [
    { "value": -100, "color": "blue" },
    { "value": 0,    "color": "green" },
    { "value": 100,  "color": "red" }
  ],
  "steps": 64
}
```

- The legend should show the custom scale.
- Values outside the stops' range should saturate, as they do today.
- An alternative with the same effect is to derive the colors from the field's thresholds or color mode.

From reading `public/app/plugins/panel/heatmap`, this looks contained. `quantizeScheme()` in `palettes.ts` already returns a plain `string[]` palette. `valuesToFills` and the `ColorScale` legend consume only that array. A custom mode would add a branch there, a `stops` field in `panelcfg.cue`, and a stops editor in `module.tsx`. I'm willing to contribute a PR if the approach is acceptable.

**Who is this feature for?**

Dashboard authors who use heatmaps for signed or diverging quantities, such as forecast bias or error, deviation from target, and delta vs. a baseline. It also helps anyone who needs semantically fixed colors (for example green = nominal), as in SLO or latency heatmaps.

Environment: Grafana 12.3.3, heatmap with `calculate: false`.
issues.title: Heatmap: support custom color scales (e.g. zero-centered diverging) for the color scheme

issues.body:
## Problem

Text v2 templates should be able to reuse Grafana field display configuration directly in Handlebars: thresholds, value mappings, and other value formatting that is not currently accessible. Authors should not have to duplicate these rules in template conditions or hard-code colors.

The current Handlebars row context keeps raw values and exposes formatted strings under `fmt`, using the field display processor. This already provides formatted text, including mapping labels, units, and decimals where configured. However, converting the display result to a string loses structured information such as threshold/value-mapping colors. There is no dedicated helper exposing the full display result. This request extends the existing support rather than treating all formatting as missing.

## Desired behavior

- Use the field's resolved threshold or value-mapping color when styling a value.
- Access mapped text and other relevant display properties, including formatted text and unit prefix/suffix, while retaining raw values for comparisons.
- Respect field overrides and Grafana's existing display semantics, including mapping-versus-threshold precedence.
- Make this available when iterating rows and frames in Handlebars, as well as in Per row rendering, with unambiguous field/row resolution.

For example, a status template should be able to show the configured mapped label and color, and a numeric value should use the same unit, decimal formatting, and threshold color as other panels.

## Possible approach and performance

Evaluate dedicated Handlebars helpers that resolve field display properties on demand. Reuse Grafana's display processors rather than implementing separate threshold or mapping logic. Helper syntax and return shape are open design questions.

On-demand evaluation could avoid eagerly materializing additional display metadata for every cell. Measure this against the existing `fmt` path; helpers alone do not guarantee better performance. Consider reuse or caching within a render when several properties of the same value are requested, with correct invalidation when data, field configuration, or theme changes. Keep template compilation reusable and preserve existing row/render limits.

## Acceptance criteria

- Templates can access resolved threshold/mapping colors and formatted values without duplicating field configuration.
- Supported display properties and helper/context syntax are documented, with editor discoverability and examples.
- Raw values and existing `fmt` templates retain their behavior.
- Tests cover mappings, threshold colors, units/decimals, field overrides, null/missing values, and multiple rows/frames.
- Existing escaping and sanitization remain effective.
- Large-frame performance is evaluated, including templates that never request the new properties and templates that request several properties per value.

Parent epic: #128614. Related: #131383, #131410, #130416, #136073. Coordinate with the scoped interpolation helper proposal in #136073 to avoid overlapping APIs.
issues.title: Text v2: Expose thresholds, value mappings, and field display formatting to Handlebars

**What would you like to be added**:

Annotation queries should be evaluated in the scope of each repeated row or panel. When a row is (for example) repeated by `$deployment`, an annotation query that uses `$deployment` should run with that row's value, not the dashboard-wide value (for example "All").

**Why is this needed**:

This was requested in #39539, which was closed in 2021 because "annotation queries are global and not executed per panel" and the feature would first need #717. PR #717 (annotations on a single panel) has since been completed via #66325, but the "Show in → Selected panels" filter is static. It can't target individual repeated copies, and the query still isn't evaluated per repeat.

My example (Grafana 13.1.1 + Prometheus + Kubernetes):

 - A row is repeated by a multi-value `$deployment` variable (with "All") and contains CPU and memory time series panels.
 - An annotation query marks container restarts:
  ```promql
  increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="$namespace", container=~"$deployment"}[2m]) > 0
  ```
  - Expected: each repeated row shows only the restarts of its own deployment.
  - Actual: the query runs once with $deployment = All, so every row shows the restarts of all deployments.

The current workaround is to add the restart query as an extra series in each panel, drawn as thin bars or points on a hidden axis and a bunch more graph overrides to "fake" something that looks like an annotation.

**Who is this feature for?**

Anyone with dashboards that repeat rows or panels per service, environment, data source or volume, and who wants per-repeat event markers such as crashes, deployments or PVC resizes. The comments on #39539 show the same need.

Thank you for your time, I hope you all are having a great day. 🙂

## Outcome

Add an optional row-number gutter so users can see their position in the displayed table. This is the first implementation PR for #56884. Gate it through `table.refreshNewFeatures`; no separate enablement work is planned.

## Behavior and controls

- Generate 1-based sequential positions after sorting and filtering. Continue across pagination; virtual scrolling must not reset numbering.
- Parent numbering remains unchanged when nested tables expand. Nested tables use independent numbering. Footers are not numbered.
- Store the configured visibility default in panel options. Provide a dedicated show/hide control in the columns sidebar; interaction updates table view state without modifying transformations or saving the dashboard.
- Keep the gutter outside the ordinary reorderable, hide/showable, and pinnable field list. It is fixed at the leading edge, frozen, nonresizable, nondraggable, nonreorderable, and cannot be unpinned.
- Generated numbering has no sorting affordance. No gutter filtering UI in this delivery.

## Visual treatment

- Use the monospace support introduced in the latest RDG upgrade; verify the exact API before implementation.
- Use a compact, right-aligned gutter with muted text/background and a subtle separator. It must look distinct from an ordinary data column.
- Establish styling reusable by the field-backed gutter in the next PR.

## Implementation safeguards

- Use a presentation-only RDG column with a stable key and dedicated renderer. Do not insert a synthetic DataFrame field or change source-field/source-row mappings.
- Keep outer table width unchanged. Reserve gutter width inside the grid's available width, accounting for scrollbars exactly once.
- Size for the maximum result number using actual monospace metrics, padding, and borders. Set consistent width/minWidth/maxWidth.
- Include the gutter in preliminary and scrollbar-adjusted sizing, wrapping, row heights, pagination, frozen-column accounting, first-column padding, nested spans, and footer alignment.
- Audit field-dependent handlers so they do not treat the gutter as a source field.

## Acceptance and regression coverage

- Verify disabled and enabled behavior, sidebar toggling, sorting/filtering, page two, virtualization, nested expansion, and empty results.
- Verify ordinary field sorting/resizing after hiding or reordering fields, footer calculations, and data-link/source-row mappings.
- Cover digit boundaries such as 99 to 100, narrow panels, and real-browser scrollbar/wrapping behavior.
- No transformation is created, and no existing transformation pipeline is changed.

## Historical context

The earlier implementation (#62256) always prepended a synthetic field, causing source-field/display-column index mismatches that broke sorting and resizing. It also increased outer width when the number column was hidden and restarted numbering on each page. See #65461 and the revert #65470. The disabled state needs equal regression coverage.

## Out of scope

Field-backed numbering and sorting are the next PR. URL persistence and gutter filtering UI are follow-ups; structure view state to support eventual URL overrides.
issues.title: Table: Add generated row-number gutter and sidebar visibility control

issues.body:
**Why is this needed**:
Since #98722 / #99994, changing the Logs panel sort order in Explore updates the Loki query direction and re-runs the query. The reverse isn't true: changing **Direction** in the Loki query editor options does not change the panel sort order.

Nothing in the UI shows that these two settings are linked, or that the link only works one way. This is problematic because users can unintentionally do the following:

1. The user toggles the sort order to "Oldest first". The Direction silently becomes Forward.
2. Later, the user changes Direction in the query editor to Backward. The sort order stays "Oldest first".

The result mixes the two settings. When the line limit is reached, Loki returns the *newest* N lines in the range, and Explore shows them oldest-first. The list starts somewhere in the middle of the time range (the same symptom as #98131). The reverse case (Forward with "Newest first") shows the *oldest* N lines newest-first, so the top row looks like the most recent log while the real newest lines are missing.

In both cases the log-volume histogram, which has no line limit, shows the missing lines. To users, the list looks inconsistent or like a "random" selection. Nothing clearly explains why, so users end up concluding "Grafana is showing the wrong logs".

To reproduce:
1. In Explore, choose a Loki data source and a time range with more matching lines than the line limit (e.g. `{app="foo"} |= "bar"`, limit 2000, ~2100 matches).
2. Set the Logs panel sort order to "Oldest first". Note that Direction in the query options changes to Forward.
3. In the query options, change Direction to **Backward**. The query re-runs; the sort order stays "Oldest first".
4. The list shows "2000 lines shown — X% of 3h". The first row isn't the oldest matching line in the range; the oldest lines aren't in the list at all.

**What would you like to be added**:
Users should either never end up with direction and sort order disagreeing, or be clearly told when they do. Some options to consider:
- **Warning when they disagree:** when Direction is changed to something that doesn't match the current sort order, show a warning, either inline next to Direction,  as a notice above the logs list or maybe even a separate notification. For example: "Direction is Backward but logs are sorted Oldest first. With the line limit reached, you're seeing the newest 2000 lines in oldest-first order." Would also be nice to include a one-click "Match sort order" action.
- **Two-way sync:** changing Direction in the query editor also updates the panel sort order. 
- **Make the sync visible:** when the sort toggle changes the query direction, say so (e.g. a toast: "Query direction set to Forward to match Oldest first"). 
- **Line-count text that names the direction:** e.g. "Showing the oldest 2000 lines, sorted newest first."

Environment: Grafana v13.2.5, Loki data source plugin v13.2.5, Loki v3.5.5.
Related: #91904, #98722, #99994, #98131, #135687

**Who is this feature for?**
Anyone using Loki in Explore, especially users who search for a string over a time range with more matches than the line limit.
issues.title: Explore/Loki: warn when query Direction and logs sort order disagree (the sync only works one way)

issues.body:
## Problem

A Splunk query ending in `timechart ... by <field>` returns frames with no `labels`. In Grafana Alerting, Reduce → Threshold then names instances `Series 1..N`, so the firing instance can't be tied to the split value. The [Splunk alerting docs](https://grafana.com/docs/plugins/grafana-splunk-datasource/latest/alerting/#multi-dimensional-alert) say `timechart ... by host` creates one alert instance per host, which doesn't happen today.

`stats ... by <field>` produces labelled instances, but it isn't a time series. `bin _time span=1m | stats count by _time, <field>` fails with `input data must be a wide series but got type long`.

## Reproduction

Grafana 12.4.2 and 13.0.1, `grafana-splunk-datasource` 5.8.30.

1. Create a Grafana-managed alert rule on Splunk with `index=_internal | timechart span=1m count by sourcetype`.
2. Add a Reduce expression, then a Threshold expression.
3. Evaluate. Instances are `Series 1..N`, and Query inspector shows no `labels` key.

## Questions to resolve

- **Breaking change:** Adding labels changes instance identity, which can affect silences, notification routing, and alert state for existing rules. Should this be opt-in or gated?
- **Alert vs. panel behavior:** If we really want to avoid possible breaking changes, we can add a toggle to format for alerts
- **Scope:** Limit to Splunk `timechart`/`mstats` split results, or treat it as a generic auto-labeler?
- **Label key:** Should it be the `by` field name? Raw SPL doesn't currently give the framer that name, and multiple `by` fields would each need a label.
- **Series naming:** Keep current field names and add labels, or move split values into labels Prometheus-style? The second option changes existing panel legends.
- **Ordering:** `Series N` follows Splunk's top-N ordering, which shifts with `limit` and `useother`.

## Current workaround

Use `stats ... by` with a string column for alert rules.
issues.title: Splunk: investigate labels for `timechart ... by` results in alerting

issues.body:
**Why is this needed**:

Grafana records that an alert rule was provisioned, and it keeps edits on that rule with the provisioning source. It does not record where that source is. API provisioning, file provisioning, and tools that call the provisioning API, including Terraform, OpenTofu, and Pulumi, all look the same on the rule. A client that can read the rule can say that it is managed elsewhere. It cannot point a person at the repository or file that owns it.

**What would you like to be added**:

An optional `sourceUrl` on a provisioned Grafana-managed alert rule.

- The value is an `http` or `https` URL with a host, no userinfo, and at most 2048 characters.
- It is stored with the rule's provenance, not as an alert annotation. Annotations are copied onto firing alerts.
- The provisioning API accepts it on create, update, and rule-group replace. An empty or omitted value clears the stored URL on the next apply.
- A non-empty URL is rejected when the rule is not provisioned (`X-Disable-Provenance`, or no provenance on the app-platform object). Clearing provenance clears the URL.
- Reads that already return `provenance` also return `sourceUrl`: the provisioning API, including export, the ruler `grafana_alert` object, and the Prometheus rules API. Those read models do not accept the field on write.
- The app-platform AlertRule and RecordingRule expose the same value as the existing `grafana.app/sourcePath` annotation.
- Recording rules that share the alert-rule provisioning payload get the same field. Contact points, routes, templates, dashboards, data sources, and SLOs are unchanged.

**Who is this feature for?**

Operators who manage Grafana alert rules from an external source, and API clients that need to show a link back to that source.
issues.title: Alerting: Add an optional source URL to provisioned alert rules

issues.body:
**Why is this needed**:

Consider the following scenario: 

* A system with many sensors each with their own ENUM variable type (e.g. type1 = {TRUE, FALSE}, type2 = {PENDING, COMPLETE, STALE, UNKNOWN}, etc.)
* Each ENUM state _name_ corresponds with an integer state _value_. The numeric value/state mappings correspond with a given type; values always start at 0.
* An API that returns multi-frame timeseries data containing the above described data, containing various enum typed variable data. 
* A Grafana "state timeline" visualization depicted state value and name is desired. 

A multi-frame timeseries data sample (generated from an API call, extracted from JSON data): 
| SensorKey | Timestamp| State | Label |
| -----------|--------|-----|-----|
|sens1 | 2026-01-01T12:00:00 | 0 | FALSE |
|sens2 | 2026-01-01T12:00:00 | 0 | UNKNOWN |
|sens3 | 2026-01-01T12:00:00 | 0 | NEW |
|sens1 | 2026-01-01T12:01:00 | 1 | TRUE |
|sens2 | 2026-01-01T12:01:00 | 1 | WORKING |
|sens3 | 2026-01-01T12:01:00 | 0 | NEW |
|sens1 | 2026-01-01T12:02:00 | 1 | TRUE |
|sens2 | 2026-01-01T12:02:00 | 2 | PENDING |
|sens3 | 2026-01-01T12:02:00 | 0 | NEW |
|sens1 | 2026-01-01T12:03:00 | 1 | TRUE |
|sens2 | 2026-01-01T12:03:00 | 2 | COMPLETE |
|sens3 | 2026-01-01T12:03:00 | 4 | EXPIRED |

Currently, the "prepare time series" transform (set to multi-frame data) only supports integer values. This works for the above data only if state names are not required. 

A possible workaround is to use the "value mappings" configuration; however, this quickly becomes cumbersome when multiple variables with many states are involved. Furthermore, this is only able to map a single integer to a string; this doesn't work when different enum types re-use different numbers to represent different state names. 

Another workaround is to split the query into multiple (one sensor each), but this is also cumbersome for similar reasons. 

**What would you like to be added**:

The prepare time series transformation stage should be enum-aware (or able to cope with strings). The "convert field type" transform (choosing the "label" column and enum type) can be used to "preprocess" the string into the expected enum type if necessary. 

Perhaps there needs to be some user-specified options, to tell the transform block which are the key, time, and value columns.

**Who is this feature for?**

Any user of advanced time series capabilities.

(Grafana Enterprise [free] v12.4.14 running on Windows 11 or RHEL)
issues.title: "Prepare time series" transform should support enums and strings

**Why is this needed**:

Allow dashboards referencing centrally managed cross-dashboard (global) variables to save their own selected values as dashboard defaults.

**What would you like to be added**:
In environments with many dashboards, centrally managed variables help reduce duplication and simplify maintenance.

However, different dashboards may need different default selections for the same shared variable.

Each dashboard should retain its saved selection when reopened, without changing the global variable definition or affecting other dashboards.

**Grafana version**: 13.3
**Edition**: Grafana OSS
**Feature**: Cross-dashboard variables (grafana.dashboardGlobalVariables)
issues.title: [Feature Request] Support dashboard-specific saved values for global variables
